items.title: Two equivalent descriptions of a point of finite type of an algebraic stack

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a point of an algebraic stack is of finite type exactly when it can be represented by a locally finite type morphism from the spectrum of a field, which is also equivalent to being the image of a closed point under a smooth morphism from a scheme (author lemma at source lines 3655-3665, label lemma-point-finite-type). The proof (source lines 3667-3694) proves the easy direction by composition permanence and the converse by producing a finite type point in the fibre of a presentation and pushing it down to a closed point after shrinking (proof lines 3667-3693). The production of the finite type point in the fibre is the substance. H3.
